about: What the real-life runs of 0.18.2 on 2026-10-12 read: the model matrix on the direct keys, each failure with the cause that was read, and what a job needs to replay a finding on its own build. Data for the jobs that own the fixes; nothing is fixed in this branch. Where something was not read, it says so.

findings.what: A request that comes back with no usage is shown as "the response did not complete" with the log line "Models & Agents is not available in this build.", and booked at its whole reservation, whether the provider refused it (xAI 400, Anthropic 400, OpenRouter 404) or accepted it (Mistral 200).

exec reserves the model's whole output limit and has no option that lowers it. A budget that is too small is refused with "The next request exceeds the remaining budget.", which does not say how much is needed.
findings.numbers: reservations-2026-10-12.json: the product's own reservation for 347 models, each read with a budget of one millionth of a dollar that the product turned away before sending (exit code 5, budget_exceeded, usage.requests 0, no last response); a 348th row is Meta's contributor model, whose refusal writes no claim. A hard budget of $3.00 does not admit 8 of the 46 direct models: claude-fable-5 and claude-fable-5-1 $11.31072; claude-opus-5, claude-opus-4-8, claude-opus-4-7 and claude-opus-4-6 $5.65536; claude-opus-5-5 $4.524288; claude-sonnet-4-6 $3.393216. Six of them are above the default daily budget of $5.00 by themselves. None of the 301 cheap reseller models read is above $3.00; the 88 dear reseller models were not read.

findings.what: A run turned away for its budget sent nothing, and its reservation is left in the daily ledger with no settlement: it counts against the day. Two refusals of a dear model fill the default $5.00, and every later run that day is stopped before it sends; on a provider's route the person reads "Internal error: Models & Agents is not available in this build.", on the Meta route "Stopped: the next request (about $0.1082) would pass the session budget of $5.00 ($4.96 used). It was not sent." (the daily budget, called the session budget).
replay: Use a new, empty home, so that no real day's ledger is touched. Any Anthropic key; an account with no credit cannot be charged and shows the same.
muse-spark-code-acp providers add --preset anthropic --as demo --model claude-sonnet-5-5 --key-stdin   (the key on standard input)
muse-spark-code-acp exec --backend modelApi --provider demo --model demo/claude-sonnet-5-5 --max-requests 1 --max-budget-usd 0.25 --output jsonl "Reply with the one word OK."
Seen: exit code 5; result status budget_exceeded, usage.requests 0, ledger.refusal budget, ledger.lastResponse null, error "The next request exceeds the remaining budget."

Seen in <data folder>/paid-daily/budget-journal/<64 zeros>/<day>/claims/<claim id>/claim.json: version, scopeId, claimId, ownerId, sessionId (the day), accountId (64 zeros), reservedUsd "2.262144"; no settledUsd.
The same exec again: a second claim with the same fields. $4.524288 of the day's $5.00 is held; nothing was sent.

The same exec with --max-budget-usd 3.00, which is enough for this model: exit code 4, status failed, usage.requests 0, error "Internal error: Models & Agents is not available in this build."; its claim has reservedUsd "2.262144", settledUsd "0", hasUnknownCost false.
In another new home the last command alone is sent to the provider (usage.requests 1).

findings.what: A request that was sent and came back with no usage also leaves its claim in the daily ledger with no settlement (windows-2026-10-12-matrix-direct: six such requests, six unsettled claims, $5.541720). The product's README describes that as intended for a request without verified usage.
A budget refusal on the Meta route writes no claim in the daily ledger; a refusal on a provider's route does.
providers add --preset openrouter prints the provider, where code goes, the models and "Added …", and nothing about privacy. Every request then carries provider: {zdr: true, allow_fallbacks: true}.
findings.numbers: openrouter-zdr-listing-2026-10-12.json: by OpenRouter's own listing of zero-data-retention endpoints (GET /api/v1/endpoints/zdr, 941 endpoints), 94 of the 306 models the product offers for the stored key have no such endpoint, matched by exact id: 13 ":free" variants, 18 "~" aliases, 63 others.

findings.what: The product offers the models its catalogue prices and hides the rest: of 1,036 ids the stored keys list, 457 are offered. The Anthropic key lists claude-haiku-5-5; the product does not offer it. The stored Gemini key is refused for its shape, so none of its models can be used. No command prints the models a key lists (providers test prints their number).

theRunsOwnMistakes: Reading the reservations, the script dropped the mark of the models listed at no price. Such a model has a reservation of $0, so the product took the budget of one millionth of a dollar and sent: two requests left (zai-org/GLM-4.7-Flash through Hugging Face, completed, $0; inclusionai/ling-3.1-flash through OpenRouter, one request, answered 429, $0). The script stopped each route at once and no longer asks those models.

The first matrix attempt climbed a ladder of budgets, each refusal holding the model's reservation: it filled the day on the first model and sent nothing (windows-2026-10-12-matrix-direct-first-attempt).

The runner derived a sum "turned away before sending" from the daily ledger's unsettled claims; those claims are whole reservations of requests that were sent and came back with no usage. The four records written with that sum (matrix-direct, matrix-direct-rest, matrix-grok-4.7, cancel-rest) are restated and say so; the runner now records what the ledger holds and counts the refusals it asked for.
